Formulation
Stress from demanding job as a primary school teacher may contribute to physical symptoms, such as a dry and itchy rash potentially linked to dermatitis. The rash developed after swimming, which could be an irritant, along with work stress.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Stress-related skin condition/dermatitis
- Patient Goal(s): Relieve skin symptoms (itchiness and dryness)
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage dermatitis symptoms; address stress factors
- Actions (Patient): Apply emollients, consider OTC antihistamines, monitor symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis, prescribe steroid cream, review symptoms in follow-up

Secondary Problem: High work-related stress
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce work-induced stress
- Clinical Goal(s): Support stress management techniques
- Actions (Patient): Implement stress-reducing activities; monitor the impact of stress reduction on symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Discuss stress management strategies

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Dermatitis management
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased itchiness, spread of rash
- Coping Strategies: Utilize prescribed treatments, engage in stress-reducing activities
